subject: Post-demo: acceptance thresholds, prompt bundle & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@heliopay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliopay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T21:07:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: acceptance thresholds, prompt bundle & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so the HelioPay team has everything in one place.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary flows: refund dispute triage and reconciliation summarization (high precision required).
- Targets you shared: end-to-end latency < 350ms p50, hallucination tolerance very low, and acceptance criteria around parity to your current proprietary baseline.
- You'll run an internal benchmark on our sample prompt set and share results by EOD Wed.

What I'm attaching / linking: prompt bundle v1 (canonical prompts + negative examples), the benchmark summary CSV from our internal runs on the three candidate open families, and a short doc with proposed acceptance gates (acceptance_gates_mop_v2.md).

Proposed acceptance thresholds (draft; requested during call):
- Task-level accuracy parity: open model system must be within 3 percentage points of your baseline on the labeled dispute triage set (macro accuracy).
- Hallucination FPR (entity hallucination): <= 1.0% on the synthetic hallucination suite.
- Format/structure: generated reconciliation tables must match the schema in >97% of cases (automated schema validator).
- Regression window for rollout: no more than 5% relative drop in problem-weighted F1 across critical intents during a 7-day canary.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
1) HelioPay runs our prompt bundle + your baseline on the shared benchmark (Alex) — target: 2026-08-11 EOD.
2) Redwood to prepare a short adapter fine-tuning plan if parity is not met for intent classification (Marissa) — draft by 2026-08-12.
3) Schedule a follow-up to review gaps and possible quantization tradeoffs (Sean) — propose times for 2026-08-13 AM PT.

If you want, we can also supply a small labeled seed (250 examples) to assist quick adapter tuning — say the word and we'll upload it to the Drive link.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: postcall_prompt_bundle_v1.zip, benchmark_summary_20260807.csv, acceptance_gates_mop_v2.md

From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@heliopay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliopay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T21:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: acceptance thresholds, prompt bundle & next steps

Thanks Karthik — solid recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- The "proprietary baseline" we referenced is our in-house ensemble (rule + fine-tuned LSTM + heuristics). For fairness, we'll run both the ensemble and our current LLM-starter config side-by-side.
- For the hallucination metric, can you point to the test harness you used so we can ensure parity in instrumentation?

We'll start on the benchmark now and should have the CSV back to you by 2026-08-11 EOD. If we see a big delta on the triage task, we'll also run a quick ablation to isolate prompt sensitivity.

— Alex
Head of Automation | HelioPay

On Mon, Aug 9, 2026 at 21:07 Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Martin <alex.martin@heliopay.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T00:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: acceptance thresholds, prompt bundle & next steps

Adding a couple details from the eval side that should help HelioPay instrument the comparisons:

1) Benchmark harness and scoring
- The CSV in the Drive includes both macro and micro metrics, plus the raw model outputs for the 1,200-sample dispute set we agreed on. Use the column "hallucination_flag_v2" for entity hallucination checks — that was our lightweight heuristic plus manual review on a 150-sample seed.
- We also provide a small prompt-robustness bucket: canonical prompt + 4 perturbations. When you run the baseline and the open model, please evaluate across all 5 prompt variants and report mean +/- std. Parity should be judged on the mean.

2) Quick model recommendations given today's call:
- Candidate A (open family): Strong out-of-box intent recall, low latency when quantized; needs adapter for slot-filling precision.
- Candidate B (open family): Best hallucination profile but slightly higher token cost.
- Proprietary baseline: still tops for schema compliance without additional prompting.

3) If parity gap is <= 3 points on triage but schema compliance lags, suggest a small adapter + constrained decoding policy (we can provide a tuned decoding config). That approach has repeatedly closed ~1.5–3 pts in our recent pilots.

I'll draft the adapter plan and a sample training schedule; Karthik, I'll loop you in on the recommended hyperparam ranges.

Marissa
Senior ML Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: benchmark_summary_20260807.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Alex / Priya — quick scheduling note and a small ask from infra: can you grant our team Viewer access to the benchmark folder so we can upload our run artifacts and keep versions in sync? Link in the original email is currently viewer-only for external accounts.

Proposed 30-min follow-up slots (all PT):
- 2026-08-13 09:00–09:30
- 2026-08-13 11:00–11:30
- 2026-08-14 08:30–09:00

If you're comfortable sharing initial CSVs, Marissa will do a quick pass and produce a short delta report ahead of the call. If HelioPay prefers, we can also spin a canary with the top open candidate in a sandbox for a night and capture live metrics.

Thanks — Sean
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
